structures.name: Frontal Lobe
structures.about: The most rostral lobe of the cerebrum, in front of the central sulcus. It houses the motor cortex and, at its rostral tip, the prefrontal areas involved in planning and the regulation of behavior.

structures.name: Parietal Lobe
structures.about: The lobe caudal to the central sulcus and rostral to the occipital lobe. It integrates somatosensory information and contributes to spatial awareness.

structures.name: Occipital Lobe
structures.about: The most caudal lobe of the cerebrum. It contains the primary visual cortex.

structures.name: Occipital Pole
structures.about: The caudal tip of each cerebral hemisphere.

structures.name: Cerebellum
structures.about: The cerebellum is a hindbrain structure that coordinates voluntary movement, balance, and motor learning.

structures.name: Insula
structures.about: Cortex buried in the depth of the lateral sulcus, which in the sheep is called the sylvian (or pseudosylvian) sulcus, overlapped by the surrounding lobes. It contributes to visceral sensation and autonomic control.

structures.name: Temporal Lobe
structures.about: The ventrolateral lobe of the cerebrum, below the lateral sulcus, called the sylvian (or pseudosylvian) sulcus in the sheep. It carries auditory cortex and, deeper, the hippocampus.

structures.name: Rhinencephalon
structures.about: The "olfactory brain". The ventrolateral cortex ventral to the rhinal fissure. Prominent in the sheep brain.

structures.name: Rhinal Fissure
structures.about: The groove along the ventrolateral surface separating the rhinencephalon below from the neocortex above.

structures.name: Pons
structures.about: The pons is a brainstem structure that relays signals from the cerebrum to the cerebellum. Ascending and descending tracts also pass through it, carrying signals to and from the cortex.

structures.name: Medulla
structures.about: The caudal-most region of the brainstem, regulating autonomic functions such as breathing, heart rate, and blood pressure.
